chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is befitting for the first-timer that he should shave; and if he had (already) performed Hajj (before), then if he so desires he can shorten, and if he so desires he can shave.
He (peace be upon him) said: And when he adheres his hair or curls (braids) it, so upon him is the shaving, and the shortening is not for him.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: First-time pilgrim (one who has not performed Hajj before)
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: To shorten (the hair, not fully shaving)
key_terms.لَبَّدَ: To adhere or tie up (hair, typically in braids)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in hair cutting rulings for first-time versus repeat Hajj pilgrims?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of hair removal post-Hajj, distinguishing between the obligatory shaving for first-time pilgrims (al-ṣurūrah) and the optional shortening for those returning, while mandating shaving if hair was braided or tied during Ihram. It reflects the Imami scholarly emphasis on the completeness of the ritual act, linking physical grooming to the spiritual perfection of the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is befitting for the first-timer that he should shave; and if he had (already) performed Hajj (before), then if he so desires to he can shorten, and if he so desires to he can shave’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And when he adheres his hair or curls (braids) it, so upon him is the shaving, and the shortening is not for him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is proper for al-Sarura (one who performs al-Hajj for the first time) to shave his head, but if he has already performed al-Hajj he then may shave or do Taqsir (cutting some hair or fingernails and so on).’
He (the Imam) has said that if one has felted or braided his hairs, he must shave.’”
